statements.t: “The third quarter delivered the second-half acceleration we anticipated,” said Mark L.
Looking to the fourth quarter, we expect to benefit from continued VEVYE and TRIESENCE growth, IHEEZO’s historically strongest period, and TYRVAYA’s initial revenue contribution.
Achieving our full-year revenue guidance of $350 million to $365 million will require strong execution, but we continue to believe it is achievable.”
Baum continued, “We expect the fourth quarter to be Harrow’s strongest on record and that second-half revenue will exceed the high end of what we contemplated in March.

That said, our updated Adjusted EBITDA outlook reflects both the first half operating shortfall against our original plan and additional spending to accelerate our G-MELT NDA submission, advance important development programs, and integrate TYRVAYA.
We expect more than $33 million in fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA, bringing our full-year outlook to more than $40 million.
To be clear: our amended Adjusted EBITDA outlook is a floor, and we believe there is opportunity to exceed it.”
• G-MELT: Completed a pre-NDA meeting with the FDA; the Company expects to submit its NDA before the end of this year, meaningfully earlier than previously anticipated.
Initial clinical data is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 with a more robust interim read to be provided at our upcoming Investor's Day presentation in New York in March of 2027.
A replay of the webcast will be available on the Company’s website for one year.

In addition to the Company’s results of operations determined in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), which are presented and discussed above, management also utilizes Adjusted EBITDA, an unaudited financial measure that is not calculated in accordance with GAAP, to evaluate the Company’s financial results and performance and to plan and forecast future periods.

The Company is unable to provide a reconciliation of projected Adjusted EBITDA to expected results due to the unknown effect, timing and potential significance of expenses and the tax effect of such expenses.

risks.t: risks related to: liquidity or results of operations, including our ability to achieve revenue and Adjusted EBITDA guidance
the integration of TYRVAYA and the outcome of discussions with the licensor of VEVYE regarding the TYRVAYA acquisition
our ability to realize revenue from ex-U.S. commercial arrangements
competition from pharmaceutical companies, outsourcing facilities and pharmacies

statements.t: We believe we have built a tangible and intangible infrastructure that will allow us to scale revenues efficiently in the near and
We expect TYRVAYA to begin contributing to our results in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Based on our current expectations, we anticipate that TYRVAYA will contribute in excess of $30,000,000 of revenue in 2027, and that we will incur approximately $20,000,000 of new annual operating expenses primarily as a result of the expansion of our commercial organization, marketing activities and incremental quality, supply chain and serialization costs.

We expect TYRVAYA product gross margin, before amortization of acquired intangible assets and the effect of recognizing acquired inventory at a stepped-up value, to be generally consistent with the gross margin we realize on our current branded ophthalmic portfolio.

We do not expect the level of TYRVAYA revenue we currently anticipate for 2027 to be sufficient to achieve the first net sales milestone under the purchase agreement, which is measured over the twelve months ending December 31, 2027.
We expect TYRVAYA cost of sales to be driven principally by three items.

The third is the recognition in cost of sales of the step-up in inventory value associated with the accounting for an asset acquisition, which will result in a higher cost per unit than our historical experience as that inventory is sold and which we do not expect to recur once the acquired inventory has been sold.

The increase in selling, general and administrative expenses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025 was primarily due to increased personnel-related costs, including stock-based compensation, and consulting expenses, of $11,629,000 and $31,591,000, respectively, largely as a result of an increase in our headcount in sales, marketing and other departments,…

We believe that cash and cash equivalents of $75,336,000 at September 30, 2026, together with cash generated from operations, will be sufficient to sustain our planned level of operations, capital expenditures and the TYRVAYA payments described below for at least the next 12 months.

However, we may pursue acquisitions of products, drug candidates or other strategic transactions that involve large expenditures or we may experience growth more rapidly or on a larger scale than we expect, any of which could result in the depletion of capital resources more rapidly than anticipated and could require us to seek additional financing to support our operations.
We do not currently expect any milestone payment to become payable with respect to 2027.

We expect to use our current cash position and funds generated from our operations and any financing to pursue our business plan, which includes developing and commercializing drug candidates, compounded formulations and technologies, integrating and developing our operations, pursuing potential future strategic transactions as opportunities
We expect future cash needs to be provided by operating activities, but our forecasts may not be accurate, and our plans may change.

As of October 31, 2026, Moody’s Investors Service maintained a Long-Term Corporate Family Rating of B3 for Harrow, Inc. with a Stable Outlook and Fitch Ratings maintained a Long-Term Issuer Default Rating of B- with a Stable Outlook for Harrow, Inc. and a rating of B for our senior unsecured notes due September 2030, with a Recovery Rating of RR3.
